name: Apportionment of input tax credit — section 17(1) to (4) and (6)
definition: Where goods or services are used partly for business and partly for other purposes, credit is restricted to the input tax attributable to business purposes. Where they are used partly for taxable supplies (including zero-rated) and partly for exempt supplies, credit is restricted to the input tax attributable to the taxable supplies. The value of exempt supply for that second test is prescribed and includes supplies on which the recipient pays tax on reverse charge, transactions in securities, sale of land and, subject to clause (b) of paragraph 5 of Schedule II, sale of building. A banking company, financial institution or non-banking financial company supplying deposit, loan or advance services may instead take a flat fifty per cent. of eligible credit each month and let the rest lapse.
why_it_exists: Credit is the tax on inputs that feed taxable output. Inputs that feed private use or exempt output never produce output tax, so crediting them would refund tax that was never going to be recovered. Section 17 draws that line.
inputs: total input tax for the period
the split of use between business and non-business purposes
the split of outward supplies between taxable, zero-rated and exempt
value of exempt supply, as prescribed
for banks and NBFCs, whether the fifty per cent. option has been exercised
outputs: the admissible portion of input tax credit
preconditions: credit is otherwise available under s.16 and not blocked by s.17(5)
the same input feeds more than one use, or more than one supply category
exceptions: GST-ITC-17-3-EXPL — CONFLICT: the Schedule III carve-out from the value of exempt supply differs between the two locally held sources
common_mistakes: treating zero-rated supplies as exempt — s.17(2) groups zero-rated with taxable, not with exempt
omitting reverse-charge inward supplies from the value of exempt supply, which s.17(3) requires to be included
omitting sale of land and sale of building from the value of exempt supply
a bank switching out of the fifty per cent. option mid-year, which the first proviso to s.17(4) forbids
icai_references: NOT APPLICABLE — statutory apportionment, not an accounting allocation policy
evidence_required: outward supply values split by taxable, zero-rated and exempt
a defensible basis for the business versus non-business split
for a bank or NBFC, the record of the option exercised for the financial year
confidence_factors: weak when the business versus non-business split rests on estimate rather than a measured basis

UNKNOWN — source is the Act as updated 31-08-2021; later amendments not held locally
validation_checks: reverse-charge inward supplies, securities transactions, sale of land and sale of building are all inside the exempt-supply value
zero-rated supplies are grouped with taxable supplies, never with exempt
the bank fifty per cent. election, once made, is unchanged for the remainder of the financial year
examples: a registered person makes taxable and exempt supplies from shared premises; the input tax on rent is restricted to the taxable share under s.17(2)
counterexamples: an exporter making only zero-rated supplies — s.17(2) does not restrict him, because zero-rated supplies sit on the taxable side of the test

evidence.quote: Where the goods or services or both are used by the registered person partly for the purpose of any business and partly for other purposes, the amount of credit shall be restricted to so much of the input tax as is attributable to the purposes of his business.

Where the goods or services or both are used by the registered person partly for effecting taxable supplies including zero-rated supplies under this Act or under the Integrated Goods and Services Tax Act and partly for effecting exempt supplies under the said Acts, the amount of credit shall be restricted to so much of the input tax as is attributable to the said taxable supplies including zero-rated supplies.

The value of exempt supply under sub-section (2) shall be such as may be prescribed, and shall include supplies on which the recipient is liable to pay tax on reverse charge basis, transactions in securities, sale of land and, subject to clause (b) of paragraph 5 of Schedule II, sale of building.
The Government may prescribe the manner in which the credit referred to in sub-sections (1) and (2) may be attributed.
